_comment: Decides which clio.mcp.e2e fixtures a pull request has to run on TeamCity (Team_Atf_ClioMcpE2eTests).
Consumed by .github/scripts/Select-McpE2eTestFilter.ps1 from .github/workflows/teamcity-mcp-e2e.yml;
guarded by clio.tests/McpE2eSelectionCoverageTests.cs. Rules, in order, per changed file:
1. ignoredPaths                       -> ignored (documentation, other projects)
2. not under relevantPaths            -> ignored
3. fullRunPaths                       -> the whole suite runs (shared infrastructure)
4. clio.mcp.e2e/<Fixture>.cs          -> that fixture
5. explicitMappings                   -> the listed fixtures
6. clio/Command/McpServer/Tools/**/X.cs -> every fixture whose source names a class declared in X.cs,
a tool-name literal declared in X.cs, or is named X*E2ETests;
zero matches -> the whole suite runs
7. other clio/**/*.cs                 -> the transitive consumer closure of the file over the product
reference graph. Every MCP tool file in that closure selects
its fixtures (rule 6); every [Verb("x")] in it selects the
fixtures that spell x out. No tool and no covered verb in the
closure -> no fixture can observe the change, nothing runs.
8. other clio/** (a data asset)       -> the product files that name the asset, then rule 7 on each
9. anything else                      -> the whole suite runs
The graph edge 'A consumes B' is textual: A's identifier set contains a type declared in B. It also
carries implementation -> interface edges, so a class reached only through the DI container is not
mistaken for dead code. Name matching over-approximates, which widens a selection and never narrows
it. registrationFiles are never traversed: every type is named there, so following them would make
every change reach every tool.
A subset larger than maxSubsetFixtures becomes a full run (command-line length; the NUnit adapter's
2000-test limit for non-category filters is far above this suite's size, revisit if it grows).
A subset whose fixtures are ALL positively McpE2E.NoEnvironment (and none Sandbox) becomes mode 'none':
nothing is queued, because that tier runs on GitHub-hosted runners (.github/workflows/build.yml, job
mcp-e2e-noenvironment) and pull-request runs on TeamCity exclude it; a fixture with no McpE2E.* tier
still needs TeamCity. The TeamCity step's default
filter is baseFilter; a full pull-request run sends baseFilter plus TestCategory!=McpE2E.NoEnvironment.
_ignoredPaths: Documentation and generated help. NOT because none of it ships - clio/help/** and clio/Wiki/**
are <Content Include> in clio.csproj and help/** is served over MCP as docs://help/command/{name}
by GetHelpResources, and cliogate/Resources/** is deployed with the package. The claim that
holds is the narrower one: no fixture in clio.mcp.e2e asserts on any of it. `grep -rn 'docs://'`
over the fixtures and Support/** returns only docs://mcp/guides and docs://mcp/references, never
docs://help/. Add a fixture that reads one of these and the path has to leave this list.
Checked BEFORE relevantPaths, so a file listed here is ignored even when the workflow's paths:
_fullRunPaths: Only genuinely global things belong here: code every MCP session executes before any tool runs,
the harness itself, and artifacts the deploy installs. Everything else under clio/ is classified
by the reference graph (rule 7) - putting a path here instead is a measurable cost, because every
pull request touching it pays for the whole suite.
_toolsWithoutFixtures: MCP tools that declare a tool name and that no fixture references. The detector runs the whole
suite for a change to any of them, because it cannot tell which tests would show the regression.
Each entry is a known coverage gap, not a permanent exemption: add the fixture and remove the line.
_entryPointsWithoutFixtures: MCP resources and prompts that no fixture names - the same coverage gap as toolsWithoutFixtures,
one entry-point kind out. Such a file never enters unreachable-product-files.txt, because the
entry-point rule escalates it to a full run instead, so without this list its cost is paid on
every change and recorded nowhere. Each entry is a known gap, not an exemption: add the fixture
and remove the line. Refresh with Select-McpE2eTestFilter.ps1 -Inventory.
_fullRunOnlyFixtures: Fixtures that exercise server-level behaviour (startup, shutdown, worker processes, HTTP routing,
progress relay) rather than one MCP tool. Their code lives entirely under fullRunPaths, so they run
in every full run and no tool file can select them. clio.tests/McpE2eSelectionCoverageTests.cs
accepts them as reachable only because they are listed here; keep the list to fixtures of that kind.
